newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - PC boom set to cheer Dixons H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - PC boom set to cheer Dixons H1.

text.p: The boom in personal computers is set to drive profits up strongly at Britain's leading electrical retailer Dixons Group Plc, which reports first half results on Wednesday, analysts said.
Demand for personal computers is also expected to bring Christmas cheer for group, which will also make a statement on trading over the holiday season.

Analysts are forecasting pretax profits of 54 to 57 million stg in the first half, which does not include Christmas. This compares with last year's 37.5 million for six months. Dividend is expected to rise to around 2.5 pence from 2.05 last time.
The retailer is expected to see upbeat like for like sales momentum, although it may be at a slower pace than the 11 percent reported for the first 18 weeks of its current year, analysts said.

The group has been one of the key beneficiaries of the surge in consumer spending in Britain and consolidation in the overcrowded electricals retail market has also worked in Dixons' favour. Gross margins could see some improvement over the second half of last year, analysts said, as Dixons has taken a less aggressive stance on interest free credit.

But there are already questions about when the boom in PC sales, which now make up about 30 percent of group turnover, will start to fade. "The market is split on when there might be a slow down," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.

Another key issue will be what impact tax changes in the annual budget in November will have on Dixons. Chancellor Kenneth Clarke proposed an increase in insurance premium tax to 17.5 percent from 2.5 percent on insurance policies sold alongside consumer durables.
Dixons' shares were hit badly at the time as investors were worried the tax move could hit sales of its extended warranties.
Analysts are looking for Dixons to clarify the position, but some analysts said this might prove difficult until the terms of the tax plans are set out in full in the Finance Bill.
